canonical_definition:
What it is. Across the surveyed work, EuroSAT is most commonly described as a satellite imagery or satellite image classification benchmark or dataset used for image classification. Some definitions narrow this to land use and land cover classification, with one description calling it a dataset and deep learning benchmark for that task, and another specifying Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 10 land use and land cover classes. A smaller line of description frames it through particular evaluation settings, such as remote sensing image understanding or the evaluation of descriptions for rare or abstract visual concepts.

What it is claimed to measure. In the recorded links, papers use EuroSAT to measure the behavioral indicator Image classification. It is linked to one behavioral indicator, Image classification, and to no constructs. Several papers describe evaluations on EuroSAT as part of image recognition or classification benchmarks, including formulations such as satellite image classification and standard benchmark datasets for multiple classification domains.

Space of uses. Papers usually position EuroSAT as one dataset within broader benchmark suites for image recognition or image classification, often alongside SVHN, CLEVR, CIFAR-100, DTD, and Oxford-Pets, with other datasets also appearing in the same evaluation setups. Definitions also show several specific roles: some papers use it to evaluate few-shot learning performance, some for zero-shot clean and adversarial robustness, and another for follow-up descriptions aimed at rare or abstract visual concepts. No measurement instrument is linked to it through the recorded relations.
